publicReleaseNotes: Orbit 0.3.0: cited deal risks with reasoned dismissal and person-approved tasks, form spam protection with a reviewed spam list, honest reply and open tracking that never lets an automatic reply stop a follow-up, every current sales category carried through export and restore, a Connected products page that names what Orbit works beside, and setup-owner removal protections. It updates 0.2.0 in place with one additive migration and keeps every row. Product screenshot: .github/assets/release/orbit-now-queue-1600.png

FORM-001.summary: Lead capture forms on the buyer's website: Published forms now refuse abusive submissions with a honeypot, a signed fill proof at least two seconds old, per-form and per-network limits and optional Cloudflare Turnstile, counting each refusal and keeping suspected spam in an erasable list a person can release; company, deal and custom-property mapping are still to come. Status: partial.
FORM-001.was: Administrators build forms such as Contact sales and Request a demo, with fields mapped to contact, company and deal properties, including custom fields (RECORD-014). Fields can be required, picklist or free text, and hidden fields can carry a fixed value or a query parameter of the embedding page that the form declares. Each published form is reviewed as exact content before publication. It is available as a hosted page on the installation origin and as an embed on the buyer's allowlisted HTTPS site domains, either framed or posting directly from that origin. Neither form sets a cookie or loads a tracking script (SIGNAL-007), and a submission from any other origin is refused. Abuse protection combines a honeypot field, a minimum fill time, per-form and per-network rate limits and optional Cloudflare Turnstile. Refused and suspected-spam submissions are counted with their reason, write no customer record, and can be released by a person from a spam list. A repeated submission key is idempotent. A submission creates or updates by exact email key (RECORD-003). A new person becomes a contact; a company is linked or created from a non-free-mail domain; and when the form says so, a deal is created in a chosen pipeline and stage (OPP-009). For an existing contact, values fill only empty fields, and changes to existing values wait as a reviewed proposal (CAPTURE-004). Consent is captured with the wording, form revision and time. A form with a marketing consent box makes the person contactable only when it is ticked. An inquiry-only form records the request as the basis for one-to-one sales follow-up, as disclosed on the form. An existing do-not-contact stop always wins. Owner assignment keeps an existing contact owner (RECORD-016). Otherwise it uses the form's rule: a fixed owner, round-robin rotation across a chosen team (skipping inactive users, persisting its position across restarts and recording the choice on the timeline) or an unassigned team queue. The owner, or the chosen users and team, receive one in-app notification per submission (NOTIFY-001), plus email or push under NOTIFY-003. The new or existing deal enters NOW with the submission as its reason (OPP-007); a lead without a deal appears in the owner's lead view (RECORD-014). Submissions are listed per form, exported (DATA-001) and erased with the contact (DATA-002). **Acceptance:** Build a Contact sales form mapping name, email, company, phone and a custom deal-size field, publish it hosted and embedded on an allowlisted test HTTPS domain, and submit from that domain both framed and by direct post: a new person, an existing contact with a changed name, a honeypot-filled bot entry, a too-fast entry, a replay and a post from a non-allowlisted origin. Verify the contact, company and deal creation, the reviewed proposal for the changed name with the stored value untouched, the consent record, round-robin owners alternating across two reps, one notification per accepted submission, NOW entry, spam and origin refusals with counts, and no cookie or tracker on either page.

OUT-013.summary: Gmail and Microsoft 365 mailbox sending: Before it ships it must now meet OUT-015's separation of provider acceptance, reported delivery, inferred open reports and genuine human replies. Status: missing.
OUT-013.was: After separate send authorization, a rep sends a reviewed one-to-one message or approved sequence step as their connected Gmail/Workspace or Microsoft 365/Outlook mailbox. The message may be composed from any permitted contact, lead, company or deal record, with or without a deal (OUT-017). The same conversation appears in Sent and returns replies to the correct contact, their company and the exactly linked deal when there is one. Signatures, approved attachments, thread references and provider message IDs are retained, and sent attachments are listed on the recipients' records under RECORD-018. Opt-out headers and the link are added only where OUT-020's setting puts them, handled at the installation origin. To, CC and BCC lists, reply and reply all follow OUT-019, sent as one provider message on the provider's own thread or conversation. Current recipient permission, unchanged-content review, quiet hours, OUT-018 per-user budgets, OUT-010 visible deferral, cancellation and ambiguous-outcome rules apply identically across mailbox and existing mail transports; a mailbox is paced per mailbox within its provider's limits (OUT-018), never by a deployment-wide throttle. A disconnected mailbox visibly blocks its sends; it never silently switches identities or transport. **Acceptance:** Connect each provider, review recipient/subject/body/signature/attachment, send once and verify provider Sent, a real recipient reply and Orbit threading; revoke before a scheduled send and cause a timeout to demonstrate visible uncertainty with no duplicate or transport switch.

OUT-015.summary: Honest open and reply tracking: Timelines keep provider acceptance, reported delivery, inferred open reports and actual human replies apart with their source and time, and automatic, foreign or ambiguous replies never stop or complete a follow-up; Orbit adds no open or click collection. Status: done.
OUT-015.was: Account and deal timelines distinguish provider acceptance, delivery, an open report and an actual human reply, retaining source and observed time. Open reports are explicitly inferred and may be unavailable or privacy-proxied; they never prove reading, intent or a human response. Reply tracking rejects automatic replies and ambiguous identity for stop/completion decisions. Gmail and Microsoft 365 report no opens or clicks through their APIs, so open and link-click evidence for Orbit-sent mail comes only from OUT-016's disclosed, opt-in per-message tracking; mail without it shows `not tracked`, never `not opened`. SIGNAL-007 otherwise remains: no covert tracking script, pixel, fingerprint or cross-site collection. **Acceptance:** Ingest accepted/delivered/open events and genuine/automatic/foreign replies; show each distinct status and provenance on the same deal, label unknown opens honestly, and verify only a genuine linked reply exits follow-up.
OUT-015.now: Account and deal timelines distinguish provider acceptance, delivery, an open report and an actual human reply, retaining source and observed time. Open reports are explicitly inferred and may be unavailable or privacy-proxied; they never prove reading, intent or a human response. Reply tracking rejects automatic replies and ambiguous identity for stop/completion decisions. Gmail and Microsoft 365 report no opens or clicks through their APIs, so new open and link-click collection for Orbit-sent mail is solely OUT-016's disclosed, opt-in per-message tracking obligation; mail without it shows `open/click not tracked`, never `not opened`. Existing unsolicited provider open/click reports are retained only as inferred historical provider evidence, explicitly labelled unreliable and possibly proxied or automated; they introduce no collection or human-reading claim (ct, 19 October 2026 06:03Z). SIGNAL-007 otherwise remains: no covert tracking script, pixel, fingerprint or cross-site collection. OUT-013 inherits these reporting/provenance and genuine-reply semantics for mailbox sending; OUT-016 inherits disclosed opt-in collection and proxy/automated classification; OUT-019 inherits genuine multi-recipient attribution; SEQUENCE-002 inherits genuine-reply exits. Each must pass the corresponding expanded journey before shipping. **Acceptance:** Ingest accepted/delivered/open events and genuine/automatic/foreign replies; show separate provider acceptance, reported delivery, inferred historical open/click reports and human replies with source and occurred/recorded time on account/contact/deal history. Duplicate reports have one effect; automatic replies, foreign senders and ambiguous threads leave scheduled follow-up unchanged, including after manual linking of nonhuman evidence. Without tracking, show `open/click not tracked`. Only a genuine exact-identity linked reply stops follow-up; add no pixel, redirect token or tracking collection.

OUT-016.summary: Disclosed per-message open and click tracking: Before it ships it must now meet OUT-015's separation of provider acceptance, reported delivery, inferred open reports and genuine human replies. Status: missing.
OUT-016.was: An administrator enables tracking for the workspace, choosing open tracking, link-click tracking or both, and the disclosure text Orbit adds to tracked mail and the workspace privacy notice. Each rep then turns tracking on or off per one-to-one message, template and sequence email step (workspace default off; a rep may set their own default on). The OUT-001 review shows the tracking state, every tracked link and its exact destination, and the approval binds that state with the content. For opted-in mail sent through any Orbit transport, including OUT-013 Gmail and Microsoft 365 mailbox sending and `mail.sender.v1`, Orbit embeds one per-message, per-recipient image token and rewrites each tracked link to a per-message redirect on the installation origin that answers 302 to the reviewed destination unchanged. Gmail and Microsoft 365 report no opens or clicks through their APIs, so these tokens are the only source of open and click evidence and Orbit claims no other. No cookie, script, fingerprint or cross-message identifier is set or read, and a token resolves only to its one message and recipient. Each open or click becomes an inferred signal (SIGNAL-006) on the contact, message and deal timeline with first and last time, count and the clicked link. Machine traffic is labelled and not counted as a human event: Apple Mail Privacy Protection and Gmail or Outlook image-proxy prefetches, security-scanner link checks within seconds of delivery, and requests before provider acceptance are classified `proxy` or `automated` with the reason. The sending rep receives a real-time in-app notification (NOTIFY-001), and optionally push or email under NOTIFY-003, for the first human-classified open and the first click on each link, deduplicated per message. Opens and clicks never satisfy ACTION-001 evidence, exit or advance a sequence, count as a reply or meeting, or raise a band to high (SIGNAL-006, SEQUENCE-002); reports show them as engagement, separate from replies. A contact can be marked do-not-track, and an administrator can switch tracking off for the workspace at once; do-not-contact, do-not-track, erasure (DATA-002) and contact deletion void that contact's tokens, so later requests still redirect the link but record nothing. Mail not sent through Orbit, or sent with tracking off, shows `not tracked`, never `not opened`. A message with more than one external recipient carries one message-level token whose events are attributed to "a recipient", and is sent untracked if any external recipient is do-not-track (OUT-019). **Acceptance:** Enable open and click tracking with disclosure, approve a tracked one-to-one message sent through OUT-013 Gmail and a tracked sequence step sent through Microsoft 365, open each in a real mail client and click a link; verify one inferred open and one click signal on the deal, a 302 to the unchanged reviewed destination, one deduplicated real-time rep notification, a proxy prefetch and a scanner click labelled automated, no cookie or script, no sequence exit or high band from the open, and `not tracked` on an untracked message; mark the contact do-not-track, erase another contact and verify nothing further is recorded.

OUT-019.summary: To, CC and BCC, reply and reply all: Before it ships it must now meet OUT-015's separation of provider acceptance, reported delivery, inferred open reports and genuine human replies. Status: missing.
OUT-019.was: **Fields.** Every one-to-one composer and every reply has To, CC and BCC fields. That covers OUT-017 composes from any record, ACTION-003 drafts, OUT-013 mailbox sends and the reply after a CAPTURE-012 acceptance. Autocomplete offers active users and the contacts the user may see under TEAM-005. The draft (ACTION-004) stores the three ordered lists, and changing any of them marks a reviewed draft stale (ACTION-005). **Who can be a recipient.** - A contact is checked against RECORD-012 at approval and again at dispatch (OUT-009). A do-not-contact recipient in any field blocks the send. The refusal names that recipient and the reason and offers to remove them, which re-renders the message for a fresh review; Orbit never drops a recipient silently. An address that belongs to a contact the user cannot see is checked the same way without revealing that record. - An internal colleague, meaning an active user's address or an address at a configured internal domain (TEAM-003), can always be added. Internal colleagues are never subject to contactability, unsubscribe or tracking, and never become customer contacts. - An external address with no record is allowed when the user types it. The review requires one explicit choice for each such address: create a contact (RECORD-001) with its contactability basis recorded (`rep-initiated conversation`, or `inbound conversation` when the address is already a participant in the thread being answered); accept that address's pending CAPTURE-012 proposal; or send to it as a one-off recipient. A one-off recipient's address and the user's stated basis are recorded on the message, no contact is created, and a later reply from that address becomes a CAPTURE-012 proposal. An address matching a retained suppression proof (RECORD-012, DATA-002) is refused in every case, without naming the erased person. **Reply and reply all.** Every captured (CAPTURE-010) or Orbit-sent thread offers Reply and Reply all. Reply addresses the latest message's sender, or its `Reply-To`. Reply all adds that message's other To and CC participants, removes every address of the replying user's own mailbox and its aliases, and de-duplicates. Earlier BCC recipients are never pre-filled. The pre-filled lists are editable and pass the same per-recipient checks. The reply stays in the thread: its subject takes `Re:`, its `In-Reply-To` and `References` point to the answered message, and it joins the provider's own thread or conversation (OUT-013). **Approval and transport.** - OUT-001 approval binds the exact To, CC and BCC lists with the subject and body, and the review shows every list in full. - OUT-013, or `mail.sender.v1`, submits the approved lists as one provider message. BCC addresses travel only in the envelope, never in delivered headers. - Opt-out follows OUT-020. By default a one-to-one message or reply carries none. When it does, a message with more than one external recipient carries no one-click header; a person's opt-out through its link sets only that person do-not-contact, or records a suppression proof for that one-off address; and an opt-out that cannot name one recipient opens an unattributed stop request instead of stopping everyone. - OUT-016 tracking on a message with more than one external recipient records message-level opens and clicks attributed to "a recipient", never to a named contact. A message with any do-not-track external recipient is sent untracked, and the review says so. - Under OUT-018 one message counts once against the sender's budget. **Where it lands.** On provider acceptance, one transaction records one timeline activity on each external recipient contact (To, CC or BCC), once on each of their primary companies and once on the linked deal (OUT-017). Each activity shows the To and CC lists, limited to what the viewer may see under TEAM-005. A BCC address appears only on that BCC'd contact's own activity and to the sender. It is never shown on another contact's, company's or deal's timeline view, in another recipient's copy, in a report or in another record's export. Internal colleagues are shown by name and get no customer activity. **Who counts as a reply.** - A genuine reply from any external recipient of the message (To, CC or BCC) threads back under OUT-004 and CAPTURE-010 onto the replier's contact, their company and the linked deal. It closes OUT-017's awaiting-response obligation and, for a deal-linked message, applies OUT-005 and OUT-007 as a customer reply. - A reply from an internal colleague is logged on the thread as internal and closes nothing. - A reply from an address with no record follows CAPTURE-012. - Sequence email steps (SEQUENCE-001) are addressed To the enrolled contact, with CC limited to the internal colleagues the step names. Under SEQUENCE-002, a genuine reply on a step's thread from any external participant, including a CC'd contact or a colleague the buyer added, exits that enrollment. **Acceptance:** Through Gmail, receive a captured thread from a contact with two CC'd colleagues, one of them unknown. Reply all from Orbit, adding the team's internal sales engineer in CC and another existing contact in BCC. Verify that the pre-filled To and CC lists leave out the rep's own mailbox; that the unknown colleague needs an explicit choice and becomes a contact with basis `inbound conversation`; that the provider records one message with exactly the approved To, CC and BCC lists and no BCC header in delivered copies; that the reply is logged once on each external contact and once on their company and the linked deal; that the BCC address is absent from the other contacts' timelines and the other recipients' copies; and that a later reply from the CC'd colleague threads back onto their contact, company and deal and closes the awaiting-response obligation. Add a do-not-contact contact in CC and see the send refused, naming them; remove them and approve the re-rendered message. Add a one-off external address and an erased contact's address: the first is sent with its basis recorded, and the second is refused without naming the person. Repeat the reply-all journey through Microsoft 365, and once through `mail.sender.v1` with one-to-one opt-out turned on, where one recipient's opt-out through the message's link stops only that recipient (OUT-020).

SEQUENCE-002.summary: Immediate sequence exits and accountable outcomes: Before it ships it must now meet OUT-015's separation of provider acceptance, reported delivery, inferred open reports and genuine human replies. Status: partial.
SEQUENCE-002.was: Before every step and atomically when a stop arrives, an enrollment exits on a genuine reply (from the enrolled contact or, on a step's thread, from any external participant such as a CC'd colleague, under OUT-019), meeting booking, configured deal-stage change, won/lost outcome, unsubscribe, permanent bounce or human stop. An automatic reply does not count as a successful customer response. Reassignment, revoked permissions and mailbox disconnect pause with a reason. AGENT-002.was: The agent joins authorized stage history, actual customer replies, decision-maker coverage, task/quote commitments and call evidence to flag a stalled or risky deal. It shows the exact missed promise, conflicting date/price or absent stakeholder, separates observations from inference, and proposes a concrete next experiment or assigned task. Evidence conflicts remain visible and the manager approves changes to stage, forecast, amount, close date and commercial commitments. Owners can dismiss a finding with a reason or adjust the rule; a confidence score alone cannot move a deal. **Acceptance:** Use deals with recent opens but no reply, a missing approver and contradictory quote/call dates; inspect precise cited risk and next action, dismiss one and approve another task, then verify no autonomous stage or forecast change.
AGENT-002.now: The agent joins authorized stage history, actual customer replies, decision-maker coverage, task/quote commitments and call evidence to flag a stalled or risky deal. It shows the exact missed promise, conflicting date/price or absent stakeholder, separates observations from inference, and proposes a concrete next experiment or assigned task. Evidence conflicts remain visible and the manager approves changes to stage, forecast, amount, close date and commercial commitments. Owners can dismiss a finding with a reason or adjust the rule; a confidence score alone cannot move a deal. A missing stakeholder means no contact is recorded in that role on the deal. The agent shows recorded roles as observations; any suggested stakeholder is a labelled inference with its source and is never written as a recorded role without a person's confirmation. Current sources are the stage's last change against its stale interval, genuine customer replies, provider open reports (labelled inferred), recorded stakeholder roles, overdue internal next actions, assigned tasks and unanswered replies, mutual commitments, the next step and logged calls, meetings and notes. The decision-maker role is required by default, and owners change a deal's required roles with an attributed reason. Conflicting recorded dates and prices come from a previewed AI check that sends only those recorded lines; every conflict must quote two lines exactly or the whole result fails, and without AI the check shows as unavailable. Findings, dismissals and approved tasks never change stage, amount, close date, forecast, stakeholders or commitments and send nothing; the owner acts as approving manager until TEAM-005.
